standard_prerequisites.name: The compatibility of sections over a quasi-compact open with filtered colimits of coproducts with injective transition maps
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof at source lines 3268-3271 as a cross-chapter pointer
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the finite subsets of the two index sets to be matched up so that the coequaliser is taken over finite coproducts.

core_obligations: Present the sheaf: the proof applies the surjection statement to the sheaf and to its square over the sheaf, obtaining a coequaliser presentation of the sheaf by two coproducts of sheaves supported on members of the basis with finite values (proof lines 3251-3264)

Match finite subsets: viewing the target coproduct as a filtered colimit with injective transition maps, the proof uses that sections over the finitely many quasi-compact opens involved commute with this colimit to find, for every finite set of indices on the source side, a finite set of indices on the target side through which both maps factor (proof lines 3265-3271)
Conclude: the sheaf is therefore the colimit of the cokernels of the maps between these finite coproducts, which are exactly the sheaves displayed in the statement (proof lines 3272-3273)
proof_roadmap: 先用 lemma-surjection 把任意层 F 写成两个「基上带有限值常层的 j_! 之余积」的余等化子。
把右侧余积看作转移映射单的滤过 colim；由准紧开集上的截面与该 colim 交换（跨章引理），对每个有限 B' 存在有限 A' 使两个映射都落在其中，于是 F 是这些有限余积间映射之余核的 colim。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement exhibits every sheaf of sets on a space with a basis of quasi-compact opens as a filtered colimit of finite coequalisers of coproducts of sheaves supported on members of the basis with finite values (author lemma at source lines 3232-3248, label lemma-filtered-colimit-constructibles). The proof (source lines 3250-3274) first presents the sheaf as a coequaliser of two infinite coproducts, then views the target as a filtered colimit with injective transition maps and uses the compatibility of sections over quasi-compact opens with that colimit to match the indices into finite subsets, so that the sheaf becomes the colimit of the finite coequalisers (proof lines 3265-3273). The index matching through the quasi-compactness hypothesis is the content. H2.
